explication:
<explanation>
1. Identify the project type and purpose  
   - Boltz is a Python-based biomolecular interaction modeling toolkit that provides both inference (structure & affinity prediction) and training pipelines. It exposes a CLI (`boltz predict` / `boltz train`) and a library (`src/boltz/...`) for data processing, modeling, and evaluation.

2. Analyze the file structure  
   - Top level  
     • CLI entrypoint: `src/boltz/main.py`  
     • Library code: `src/boltz/data` (all data preprocessing, featurization, filtering, parsing, tokenization, sampling, writing) and `src/boltz/model` (layers, losses, modules, optim, potentials)  
     • Scripts:  
       – `scripts/process` (raw → processed dataset)  
       – `scripts/train` (configuration, training driver, asset lists)  
       – `scripts/eval` (evaluation driver, metric calculators)  
     • Examples (YAML input files) and docs (usage & architecture guidance)  
     • Config files: `pyproject.toml`, `scripts/process/requirements.txt`, YAML config under `scripts/train/configs`

3. Examine the README for additional insights  
   - Two main workflows:  
     • Inference (`boltz predict`), optionally contacting an MSA server, producing structure & affinity predictions  
     • Training (currently Boltz-1, soon Boltz-2), driven by YAML configs, outputting model weights & metrics  
   - Dependencies: Python, PyPI package `boltz`, optional external MSA server, RCSB mmCIF resources

4. Designing the system architecture diagrams  
   We will produce two separate diagrams—one for Inference, one for Training—each annotated with component names, function, and block I/O lists.

   A. Inference Diagram  
   Components & I/O:  
     1. User Interface (CLI / Python API)  
        • Input: `input_path` (YAML or directory of YAML)  
        • Output: prediction job submitted to pipeline  
     2. Input Parser & Validator (`src/boltz/data/parse/*.py`)  
        • Input: raw YAML → `ParsedSpec` objects  
        • Output: standardized object with molecule identifiers & prediction types  
     3. MSA Retrieval Service  
        • Input: sequence from `ParsedSpec`  
        • Output: MSA files (A3M) or `None` if disabled  
     4. Feature Construction (`src/boltz/data/feature/featurizer*.py`)  
        • Input: raw sequence + MSA  
        • Output: feature tensors (e.g. residue indices, pairwise features)  
     5. Model Inference (`src/boltz/model/modules` + `src/boltz/model/models/boltz*.py`)  
        • Input: feature tensors, model weights  
        • Output:  
          – Structure prediction (atom coordinates)  
          – Affinity outputs: `affinity_pred_value`, `affinity_probability_binary`  
     6. Post-Processing & Writer (`src/boltz/data/write/*.py`)  
        • Input: raw model outputs  
        • Output: PDB/mmCIF files, JSON summary with affinity fields  
     7. CLI Output  
        • Input: file paths + summary  
        • Output: console logs, result files in working directory

   B. Training Diagram  
   Components & I/O:  
     1. Raw Data Sources (PDB/mmCIF, FASTA, MSA directories)  
        • Input: external repositories (RCSB, local FASTA)  
        • Output: raw data files  
     2. Data Processing Scripts (`scripts/process/*.py`)  
        • Input: raw data files  
        • Output: processed dataset shards (serialized feature files)  
     3. Training Configuration (`scripts/train/configs/*.yaml`)  
        • Input: user-selected config (e.g. `full.yaml`, `confidence.yaml`, `structure.yaml`)  
        • Output: hyperparameters, data splits (`scripts/train/assets/*.txt`)  
     4. Training Driver (`scripts/train/train.py`)  
        • Input: processed dataset, config  
        • Output: training loop initialization  
     5. Data Loader & Sampler (`src/boltz/data/sample/*.py`)  
        • Input: processed dataset shards  
        • Output: batches of feature & label tensors  
     6. Model & Loss Computation (`src/boltz/model/modules` + `src/boltz/model/loss`)  
        • Input: batch tensors, model weights  
        • Output: loss values, gradients  
     7. Optimizer & Scheduler (`src/boltz/model/optim/*.py`)  
        • Input: gradients, hyperparameters  
        • Output: updated model weights (checkpoints)  
     8. Checkpoint & Metrics Logger  
        • Input: model weights, loss/accuracy metrics  
        • Output: saved checkpoints, TensorBoard logs, evaluation on validation set

5. Architectural patterns & design principles  
   - Modular layering: clear separation between data ingestion (`data/`), model definition & training (`model/`), and orchestration (CLI + `scripts/`).  
   - Pipeline pattern: streaming data through parse → feature → model → write stages.  
   - Config-driven via YAML for experiment reproducibility.  
   - Use of external services abstracted behind interfaces (e.g. MSA server, RCSB fetcher).

6. Guidelines for tailoring the diagrams  
   - Draw two side-by-side or two stacked diagrams: one labeled “Inference Pipeline,” one “Training Pipeline.”  
   - Within each:  
     a. Use rectangular boxes for internal components, cylinders or cloud shapes for external services/data  
     b. List each box’s inputs and outputs in bullet form inside or adjacent to the box  
     c. Use arrows to indicate data flow direction  
     d. Color-code:  
        – Green for data preprocessing stages  
        – Blue for model inference/training stages  
        – Orange for CLI or orchestration layers  
        – Gray for external services

7. Diagram elements checklist  
   - Clear, human-readable labels on every component  
   - Bullet list of input and output names on each block  
   - Directional arrows with arrowheads to show flow  
   - Color coding or distinct shapes to differentiate data, compute, and external services  
   - Legend explaining colors/shapes

By following these steps and focusing on the distinct inference and training flows—each with explicit I/O annotations—you will produce a clear, accurate, and project-specific system design diagram for Boltz.  
</explanation>
